text:
lately I am visited by thoughts of that, what should I do further...? I am engaged in FX studying about 5 years. At the first stage I wished to grow rich quickly, but have got to an emotional stress and have promised myself that I will learn trade. All rest of the time I looked for something to understand sense of trade. I even was on RTM of the way in the beginning, but for some reason I didn't remain here. Sorry to hear that. You have come to a crossroads and must decide. I have been trading almost 10 years on and off and I was always looking to decipher the code of the market and RTM has finally helped me. I have a tough time dealing with lossses but RTM has helped because stop lossses are in 3-4 pip range. Everyone must in the end choose what he is comfortable with.

Trading is not actually easy at all as there is also an aspect which people don't realize is that when you are winning you might be bankrupting some other fellow who is trading on your opposite position. There is subtle vibes which pollute the consciousness which are not always clearly visible. Thereffore it is always good to give in charity and humanitarian causes.

What sometimes happens is that we get stuck into analysis paralysis. We start looking at every kink and every LS and then have a whole mess on our chart and then we take no trades. I think you need to think to yourself what do you want from forex trading. There should always be a end goal otherwise we will be wandering aimlessly. For me forex is a way to become financially independent and fulfil my desire to travel the world and give in charty to helping animals.

This distinction between best and worst is all in the mind. We are all equal but society has divided us from childhood filling our minds with the way things should so called be.

Wish you all the best in what course of action you decide to take brother.

author: einrikr
text:
Ha Constantine,

I believe that you were correct. LS = RS but not all RS are LS.

I believe that RS is Resistance/Support, yes. I think that both images you provided are correct. The RS in the right image is ftb to the LSK, but in itself, it is RS.

In essence, every Low or High is Resistance/Support. Regardless other names we give them. They are a simple way to locate kinks. You could follow a FL trail as well and you'll find that every single one of them is the break of something important. Kinks are a set of highs and lows in the end.

author: HCDE
text:
I recently made a post saying that some part of the RTM material was confusing. The answer was, more or less: "I don't see any reason for confusion"... Your point is symptomatic of RTM's core problems: it's inefficent, both for those who learn or for those who try to teach. Is it efficient that every student make the fastidious work of compiling every piece of knowledge in the journals? Is it efficient to answer some important questions in everyone journals (pretty much lost in the deep one week later) while it could be done in a centralized place, or gathered once and for all in markepedia?

Then the next question is: how can it remain so inefficient since so many years? To my opinion: because there is no interest to make it efficient for a subscription fee under 600€ in average. I like a lot the RTM concepts IF came up with and i'm very grateful to him for sharing them with us in the first place. I was very happy about RTM re-opening in 2017, i thought it was full of promises and that it would help me succeed in my project of doing another job. But the conclusion of that isn't very fancy. I drained a part of my savings & spent a lot of time studying a lot of useless stuffs, wasting a lot of time like you did, jumping from one vision to another, never finding any consistency. For sure, i'm the first responsible for that. I could & should be more clever, more organized maybe, having a more scientific approach also.... But honestly RTM has a lot of questions to find an answers for. Most people only post their success on the forum, that's human nature, but as a result, IF & RTM team think everyone is fine. But let's be very objective about RTM's achivements: How many people took their shot at cracking it, and how many succeeded to LIVE & CONSISTENT trading? What's the ratio? How good is RTM at making you a real trader? Where are these people who succeeded at RTM (and i mean RTM, not RTMA or with any help from IF)? How many are they? I'm here since several years, i don't have more than 2-3 in mind. How many people have a worst life situation after RTM than before? Obviously, i have my opinion on these questions.

I sincerely hope some of the nice people on that forum will make it, but honestly, i think most of you, like me actually, are wasting their time. That's my humble (& unpleasant) opinion.

Anyway, in everything in life there is a lesson. And the lesson in my case is: When you invest into something, investing into something that has a real reason to make you succeed.
